title: Paediatric emergency in the prehospital setting – a retrospective, monocentric data analysis
summary:
Childhood emergencies place a particular burden on emergency physicians, both professionally and emotionally. Different data sets exist on the type and frequency of these emergencies. There is a lack of meaningful data analysis for the Ulm ambulance service area, and thus a lack of a basis for needs-based training and continuing education for emergency physicians.
In addition, we want to use a special statistical analysis method known as machine learning to find out which combinations of characteristics make it necessary to call an emergency doctor in every case. Until now, the dispatching emergency call centre has usually alerted an emergency doctor in addition to the ambulance for every suspected case of a child. In the future, the results of our analysis could be used to make this procedure more needs-based.

interventions.name: All emergency doctor calls classified as paediatric for the three Ulm emergency vehicles in the period 01/01/2015–30/09/2023

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
In the record of a patient who falls within one of the following age definitions 
Neonate Up to the completed 28th day of life
Infant From the 29th day of life to the completed 12th day of life
Infant From the age of 2 years to the age of 3 years
Child From the beginning of the 4th year of life to the completed 12th year of life
Adolescent From the age of 13 to the age of 18
The definition of age groups is based on that of the German Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians. 

TAKWA protocol completed in full, suspected diagnosis clearly recognisable from the protocol.

Target clinic 'Universitätsklinikum Ulm' with the corresponding clinics such as paediatric clinic, surgical emergency room, etc.
Exclusion criteria:
Non-paediatric age as defined above
Target hospital not Ulm University Hospital
Data set incomplete
